पौरंदर, i. e. पुरंदर + अ, adj. Belonging or relating to Purandara, i. e. Indra,

 1. Descended from Puru,

. m. pl. The race of Puru, Śāk. d. 49.
 3. m. pl. The name of a people.
 --Comp.

पौरस्त्य, i. e. पुरस् + त्य, adj.
 1. Prior, first.
 2. Eastern, Bhāg.

पौराण, i. e. पुराण + अ, adj., f. णी.
 1. Relating to past ages, ancient,

पौराणिक, i. e. पुराण + इक, adj., f. की.

. Conversant with the events of former times,

पौरिक, i. e. पुर + इक, m.
 1. Citizen, Mārk.

. pl. The name of a people.

पौरुष, i. e. पुरुष + अ,
 I. adj., f. षी.
 1. Manly,
. Sacred to Puruṣa; epithet of a holy text,

. Having the measure of a man with both arms elevated and the fingers extended.
 II. [] m. The load which a man may bear,

(Kull. ? perhaps a full grown man).
 III. n.
 1. Manhood, manliness,
